messages:
anya: Quick profiling pass on the new kernel-gate hysteresis changes. TL;DR: we regressed ~12% tokens/s on mixed SM farm for seq_len ~64-192 corner cases.

anya: Repro steps I ran: boot nodes with flag `--kernel-gate-hysteresis=8` and probe workload seqlen distribution skewed to 128. Ran 5x short gen runs (50 tokens) with batching disabled.

morgan: Oof. Numbers?

anya: Paste from perf-bot: ```
model: redwood-tiny, batch=1, seq=128
old-path: 1420 tokens/s, p95=47ms
new-hysteresis=8: 1248 tokens/s, p95=52ms
regression: -12.1% tokens/s, +10% p95
notes: increased kernel-switch churn visible in device traces
```

ravi: Any indication why it's switching more? Was the hwcap probe returning inconsistent flags?

anya: That's the weird bit — device probe logs show SM feature fingerprint flipping between runs on same GPU. snippet: `capflags: SM86+TC+BF16 | SM86+TC` (i.e. BF16 bit missing on some runs).

sylvia: Could be non-deterministic read of `cuDeviceGetAttribute` from our init path if an NV driver query races with a container startup. We saw similar before with older driver 520.x. Which driver on that node?

anya: Node kernel says driver 537.21. But I also saw a transient error in the probe: `WARN hwprobe: cudaGetDeviceProperties returned inconsistent nvcc_major` right before capflags flip.

chris: If capflags flips, kernel picker can bounce between TC-optimized BF16 kernels and fallback FP32 kernels. That would explain perf loss and p95 bump due to small microbatches hitting slower kernels mid-epoch.

morgan: Can we stabilize by applying hysteresis on the capflags read, rather than on kernel choice? e.g., read device props once and cache for X minutes or until driver change.

anya: I prototyped a cheap debounce: cache capflags for 30s and treat read failures as keep-old. With that: ```
seq=128, hysteresis=8 + cap-cache=30s: 1390 tokens/s, p95=48ms (regression reduced to -2.1%)
```

ravi: Nice. But caching introduces risk if something legitimately changes (hot-plug or MIG create). We should add an explicit invalidation on a probe error or on CUDA runtime events.

sylvia: Agreed. Also we should prefer a deterministic mapping from `computeCapability` to kernel-path instead of relying on heuristic feature bits when possible. e.g., compute 8.6 -> prefer bf16 tc kernels unless driver version < X.

chris: We should add telemetry counters: #capflag-flips, #kernel-path-switches-per-minute, and correlate with p95 regressions. Then we can set an automated safety: if flips > N in T -> pin kernel by computeCapability.

anya: Filed a quick RFC: https://redwood.internal/infra/notes/hwcap-debounce (WIP). Also adding a tiny change to runtime: `--cap-debounce-ms=30000` default 0 for now.

build-bot: CI: perf test run queued with `--cap-debounce-ms=30000` on the mixed-sm perf cluster (job id perf-2026-78).

morgan: One more ask — can we surface a small log line when we pick a fallback kernel due to missing BF16/FP8 capability? e.g., `KERNEL_PICK: fallback fp32 (missing BF16)`. That will help postmortems.

anya: Good idea. I'll add structured log field `kernel_pick.reason` and include `capflags_read` snapshot.

ravi: Ok next steps: 1) Add capflags cache + error fallback (anya), 2) Add telemetry counters (chris), 3) Add structured logs for kernel picks (morgan), 4) Run extended perf job and report.

anya: I'll post results after perf-2026-78 finishes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
